subject: Clarifying isolation requirements: Dedicated vs Private VPC (post-demo)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finlogix.com>, Procurement <procurement@finlogix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying isolation requirements: Dedicated vs Private VPC (post-demo)

Alex — thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can prepare a tailored proposal.

Recap (from our demo):
- Primary goal: run inference for customer-facing features with sub-200ms p95 latency.
- Secondary goal: run occasional fine-tune/continuous-learning jobs that will touch PHI.
- Compliance: must demonstrate hardened audit logs, customer-controlled key management, and US-only residency.

Questions we need clarified to propose the right deployment mode:
1) Which workloads will process PHI? (inference only, training/ft only, or both)
2) Do you require full control of the control plane (private control plane) or is a customer-managed network attachment (VPC peering / private link) sufficient?
3) Is there a hard no on shared multi-tenant compute for PHI data, or would a dedicated pool with strict tenancy controls be acceptable?
4) Timeline: when do you need the PHI workloads isolated (POC vs production)?

Next steps from our side: I attached a short isolation-eval checklist that maps answers to recommended deployment patterns (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC / On‑prem). If you can answer the bullets above, Ben and Marissa will draft two options: (A) minimal lift — Dedicated capacity with KMS + strict tenancy controls, (B) maximal isolation — Private deployment with customer-managed control plane and HSM.

Proposed immediate action: please let me know availability for a 30-min technical follow-up this week so we can align on constraints and capture any procurement gating. I also looped Procurement for contract/PO expectations.

Attachments: isolation-eval-checklist.xlsx (excel)

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finlogix.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlogix.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying isolation requirements: Dedicated vs Private VPC (post-demo)

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline below.

1) PHI scope: both inference and the periodic fine-tune jobs will touch PHI. Inference is high-volume (customer lookups), fine-tune jobs are less frequent but must be auditable.
2) Control plane: we need a private control plane (no multitenant control plane that stores metadata outside our VPC). Network attachment alone is not sufficient.
3) Shared compute: unacceptable for PHI. All PHI processing must run in customer-owned or customer-dedicated compute.
4) Timeline: POC targeted for Nov 2025, production by Q1 2026. POC can be limited scope but must prove audit/logging + KMS integration.

Other constraints:
- Data residency: US-East only for PHI workloads.
- Audit: 7 years of read-only append logs for all inference calls that touch PHI.
- KMS: we need BYOK with HSM-backed keys (we are using AWS CloudHSM).

I've attached a short PDF (sld-isolation-requirements.pdf) that our Security team shared — it enumerates legal/compliance asks you may see during procurement. Procurement is looking for a high-level estimate and a list of non-functional checks we can use for our internal gating.

Happy to do a technical deep-dive with your solutions engineering team next week (Tue/Wed mornings eastern).

—Alex
Alex Mercer
CTO, FinLogix
alex.mercer@finlogix.com | +1 617-555-0199

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarifying isolation requirements: Dedicated vs Private VPC (post-demo)

Team — forwarding FinLogix requirements. Key takeaways: private control plane + no shared compute for PHI; BYOK/HSM; 7-year append-only logs; US-East residency; POC Nov, prod Q1-26.

Can you help map to three concrete delivery options we can present:
- Option 1: Dedicated capacity + KMS + elevated logging (lowest implementation time, medium cost)
- Option 2: Private deployment (customer control plane in their VPC) + BYOK/HSM (higher implementation time, higher cost)
- Option 3: Hybrid: Private control plane + dedicated compute pool for PHI, with a secure bridge for high-volume inference (best balance, need engineering sign-off)

Please add ballpark TTF (time-to-first-test/POC) and high-level pricing bands. Also flag any blockers (e.g., we do not support HSM-backed keys for private control plane today without an SE effort).

Adding my notes from the call as attachment (customer_psr_notes.txt). Ben — can you take point on pricing bands? Marissa/Karthik — can you own feasibility and a quick delta analysis for our private control plane + CloudHSM ask?

Thanks — will sync with Alex once we have the options.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarifying isolation requirements: Dedicated vs Private VPC (post-demo)

Got it — I can draft pricing bands and a high-level proposal. Preliminary thoughts:
- Option 1 (Dedicated): quickest to POC (~6–8 weeks), cost: mid-range (reserved GPU pool + KMS integration). Meets latency and residency, but would not be fully acceptable if customer insists on private control plane.
- Option 2 (Private): POC ~10–12 weeks, higher cost (control plane deployment + dedicated ops + HSM integration), will hit all constraints once SE-led engineering work is scheduled.
- Option 3 (Hybrid): POC ~8–10 weeks, complexity in secure bridging; likely our recommended path for customers who need control plane isolation plus efficient inference.

I'll pull together a short one-pager and schedule a 30-min Solutions Eng call — suggest Wed 6 Aug 10:00–10:30 PT. Booking link: https://cal.redwood.ai/se-ffi-finlogix. I'll attach the one-pager to the next thread.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
